data.long_meaning: One who is slaughtered, killed, or sacrificed. Parents who choose Murtah usually hope their child will grow to embody slaughtered, killed and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Murtah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Slaughtered, Killed.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Murtah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: مرتاح
in_arabic.meaning: مرتاح الشخص الذي يشعر بالراحة والاطمئنان
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مرتاح مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ر-ط-ح' والذي يعني الراحة والاطمئنان. يعتبر اسمًا يوحي بالسكينة والهدوء، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سياق الحديث عن النعيم والراحة في الجنة. يستخدم الاسم في الثقافة الإسلامية ليدل على الشخص الذي يشعر بالراحة والاطمئنان.

in_urdu.name: مرتاح
in_urdu.meaning: وہ شخص جو راحت اور اطمینان محسوس کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: مرتاح نام عربی جڑ 'ر-ط-ح' سے نکلا ہے جس کا مطلب راحت اور اطمینان ہے۔ یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں سکون اور آرام کے احساس سے وابستہ ہے۔ قرآن کریم میں اس جڑ کا ذکر راحت اور نعمت کے سیاق میں آیا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی روایت میں، یہ نام ایک ایسے شخص کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو راحت اور اطمینان کا अनुभव کرتا ہے.

in_hindi.name: मुरताह
in_hindi.meaning: वह व्यक्ति जो आराम और संतुष्टि महसूस करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुरताह नाम अरबी मूल 'र-त-ح' से निकला है जिसका अर्थ है आराम और संतुष्टि। यह नाम इस्लामी संस्कृति में शांति और सुकून की भावना से जुड़ा है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम उस व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो आराम और संतुष्टि का अनुभव करता है।

in_pashto.name: مرتاح
in_pashto.meaning: هغه کس چې راحت او ارام احساسوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: مرتاح نوم د عربي ريښو 'ر-ط-ح' څخه اخيستل شوی دی چې معنی يې د راحت او ارام دی. دا نوم د افغان او پښتن مسلمانانو په کلتور کې د سولې او آرام احساس سره تړلی دی. په پښتو ژبه کې، دا نوم د هغه چا لپاره کارول کیږي چې راحت او ارام تجربه کوي.

in_english.name: Murtah
in_english.meaning: One who feels comfort and tranquility
in_english.long_meaning: The name Murtah is derived from the Arabic root 'ر-ط-ح' (r-ṭ-ḥ), which signifies comfort, relief, and tranquility. This root is mentioned in the Quran in contexts describing the bliss and comfort of Paradise. In Islamic tradition, Murtah is a name given to someone who experiences comfort and peace. Etymologically, it relates to feelings of being soothed and eased. Historically, the name has been used across various Muslim cultures to denote a person of serene and peaceful nature.

data.cultural_impact: The name Murtah holds historical significance in Islamic traditions as it is associated with the sacrifices made during the annual Hajj pilgrimage. The ritual sacrifice of an animal, commonly a sheep, goat, or camel, is an essential part of this pilgrimage, representing Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son Ismail in obedience to Allah's command.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Murtah carries deep spiritual significance in the Islamic faith as it symbolizes self-surrender and submission to Allah. Through the act of sacrifice, the believer experiences a sense of purification and renewal, spiritually reconnecting with their Creator. By honoring this tradition, one can strengthen their faith and strive to emulate the examples of Ibrahim and Ismail, ultimately seeking nearness to Allah.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Slaughtered, Killed" symbolizes One who is slaughtered, killed, or sacrificed. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Murtah serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of slaughtered, killed.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 8, Page 241 The name Murtah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: 632 AD (10th year of Prophet Muhammad's prophethood)
historical_references.context: The Battle of Hunayn: Murtah ibn Rabahah, the chief of the Hawazin tribe, was captured by Islam and accepted Islam. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) named him 'Abd Allah ibn Murtah and gave him the title 'Murtah Ibn Rabahah al-Habashi' meaning 'Murtah the Ethiopian.'

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Hisham's Sirah Ibn Hisham, Volume 2, Page 487-488 The name Murtah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: 632 AD (10th year of Prophet Muhammad's prophethood)
historical_references.context: The Battle of Hunayn: Murtah ibn Rabahah, a chief of the Hawazin tribe, was captured by the Muslims during the Battle of Hunayn. He was originally an enemy of Islam but later accepted Islam and was granted the title 'Murtah Ibn Rabahah al-Habashi' meaning 'Murtah the Ethiopian' by the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) in recognition of his bravery and leadership skills during the battle.
